_note: Modern values: R. Chaim Naeh as tabulated on Halachipedia (Shiurim, 'Ayfah, Seah, Kav, Log': log 324 cc, kav 1296, se'ah 7776, ephah 23328; etzba 2 cm, amah 48 cm). Cross-check: Wikipedia gives the log as 6 eggs and Naeh's egg as 54 cc (6 x 54 = 324); Naeh's etzba of 2 cm agrees. NOT YET checked in Shiurei Torah itself. Ratios, checked against commentators on 2026-10-28: se'ah = 6 kav, kav = 4 log (Rashi, Chullin 99b; Steinsaltz, Eruvin 83a); letekh = 15 se'ah and kor = 30 se'ah (Rambam on Mishnah Shevuot 6:3; Rashi, Bava Kamma 58b); ephah = 3 se'ah (follows: ephah is a tenth of the kor/homer, Ezekiel 45:11). Still to read in the Mishnah text itself. MONEY: ratios in perutot: perutah 1; issar 8 (Kiddushin 1:1: a perutah is 1/8 of an Italian issar); pundion = 2 issar (16); ma'ah = 2 pundion (32); dinar/zuz = 6 ma'ah (192); sela = 4 dinar (768); maneh = 100 dinar (19,200). Issar/pundion/ma'ah/dinar ratios from the Tosefta as quoted in Sefer HaArukh, Kaf 111 (to be checked in the Tosefta); sela = 4 dinar and maneh = 100 dinar: Ketubot 1:2 and common usage (to be checked). Prices: only what the Mishnah states, with citation. METALS: perutah copper (Davidson, Kiddushin 1:1: 'a small copper coin'); issar silver (same note: 'a small silver coin'); ma'ah silver (Ketubot 5:9); pundion not stated, silver by value; dinar/zuz, sela and the maneh are silver; the gold dinar is a separate coin worth 25 silver dinar (Bartenura BM 5:1; Rashi Ketubot 93a). Photos: dry units (kav and up) use the lipless vessel with grain, small units the lipped vessel with wine. COIN PHOTOS (author-supplied, 2026-10-28; credit lines still to be supplied before public release): gold = aureus, reverse with a jug (a Roman aureus of the late Republic); silver = Tyrian silver coin, reverse with an eagle; copper = bronze prutah of Agrippa I, reverse with three ears of grain. Only sides without a person's portrait are used. Originals in data/generated_originals/coins/. The gold dinar is drawn at the size of two silver dinar (half a sela): gold was about 11.5 to 12 times silver by weight (author), and 25 / 12 is about 2 dinar-weights. LENGTH (Naeh via Halachipedia, Length > Amah, Tefach, Etzbah): etzba 2 cm, tefach 8 cm, amah 48 cm; ratios etzba : tefach : zeret : amah = 1 : 4 : 12 : 24 (zeret = half an amah = 3 tefachim; to verify in Steinsaltz). AREA: beit se'ah = 2,500 square cubits (50 x 50), from our outline of Kehati on BK 6:2; beit kav = 1/6 and beit kor = 30 beit se'ah (to verify); square metres computed from the 48 cm amah: 2,500 x 0.48 x 0.48 = 576 m2. HAND PHOTOS (author-run prompts): closed hand palm up and spread hand palm down; brackets are approximate (a real span is about 2.5 tefachim, the standard is 3). The elbow is not in the pictures, so no photo bracket for the amah. WEIGHT (silver weights of the coin-named units; Halachipedia, Money section: prutah = 1/40 gram of silver per R. Chaim Naeh, Shiurei Torah, and the Steipler; dinar = 192 prutot = 4.8 g, citing Rashi on Kiddushin 12a; sela = 4 dinar = 19.2 g; shekel = 2 dinar = 9.6 g (the page's coin table has 1 sela = 2 shekels); maneh = 100 dinar = 480 g). The Mishnah weighs in these same named units (Ketubot 5:8 a maneh of fig cakes; 5:9 five sela of thread). To verify in Shiurei Torah. Litra and kikar still to add when a mishnah needs them. DISTANCE: mil = 2,000 amot (Halachipedia, Distance of Mil); 3/4 mil = 1,500 amot (Shulchan Arukh OC 261:2); parsah = 4 mil (Arukh HaShulchan OC 459:5, quoting the Gemara: ten parsot = forty mil a day); ris = 1/15 mil = 133 1/3 amot (Shita Mekubetzet on Bava Metzia 32b, which also records other readings); metres computed from the 48 cm amah (R. Chaim Naeh): mil 960 m, parsah 3,840 m, ris 64 m. Walking time per mil: 18 min (SA OC 459:2); 22.5 or 24 (Biur Halakha). To verify the ris in the Gemara. REFERENCE BOX: hin = 12 log (Rif on Pesachim 23b: 'hin = twelve log'); bath = ephah and kor/homer = 10 bath or 10 ephah (Ezekiel 45:11 and 45:14); a dry ephah and a liquid bath are the same size. Which units are used dry or liquid is marked use: liquid / dry / both and still to be checked in the Encyclopedia Talmudit. SELA = SHEKEL (author, 2026-10-28): the weight chart has no separate shekel of 2 dinar (Halachipedia's coin table lists one); the sela is labelled 'also a shekel'; to verify in Mishnah Shekalim / Bekhorot 8:7. HAND ILLUSTRATIONS (author-run, flat style): arm shown from the elbow only (the upper-arm stub was removed and the elbow outlined); amah bracketed elbow to middle fingertip; in these pictures amah : etzba is about 24 : 1 and tefach : etzba about 4 : 1, the span is shorter than 12 etzba (approximate). Volume: one chart only (author, 2026-10-28); ephah and bath are shown stacked in the ephah slot (bath = the same size, with the lip and wine). VERIFIED 2026-10-28 (Sefaria text search): Rif on Pesachim 23b gives the whole ladder: se'ah = 6 kav, kav = 4 log, log = 4 revi'it, amah = 6 tefachim, tefach = 4 etzba (fingers); Rambam, Tefillin 9:9 gives amah = 6 tefachim and tefach = 4 fingers; zeret = half an amah (Tosafot on Menachot 97b), so 3 tefachim; beit se'ah = 50 x 50 amot (Rambam, Sabbath 16:3); sela = 4 dinar, dinar = 6 ma'ah, ma'ah = 4 issar (Rambam on Mishnah Maaser Sheni 4:3); a gold dinar = 25 silver dinar (Bartenura BM 5:1; Rashi Ketubot 93a); maneh = 100 dinar (Steinsaltz on Rambam). STILL UNVERIFIED: the sela = shekel identification and the 1/8 issar prutah chain beyond Kiddushin 1:1; beit kor = 30 beit se'ah (follows from a kor = 30 se'ah; Tosafot Yom Tov on BK 6:4 refers to Bava Batra ch. 7 for it); ris = 1/15 mil (one source); all Naeh figures (against Shiurei Torah); the 12:1 gold-to-silver ratio (author). EATING SIZES (author, 2026-10-28; the Rashi / Rambam toggle): the Rishonim dispute the zayit : beitzah ratio and the size of a peras. Rambam: kezayit = 1/3 beitzah (like his grogeret), a loaf = 6 eggs so achilat peras = 3 eggs. Rashi: a loaf = 8 eggs so achilat peras = 4 eggs; the half-beitzah zayit is attributed to Tosafot (and is R. Chaim Naeh's 27 cc). Sources found: Yeshivat Har Etzion (Berakha Acharona: Kedei Akhilat Peras), Shulchan Aruch HaRav (How much is Kdei Achilas Peras), Kessef Mishneh on Rambam Shabbat 8:4. Naeh: beitzah 54 cc (Shiurei Tzion; 57.6 with shell in Shiurei Torah), zayit 27 (earlier 28.8; lenient 17.3). Melo lugmav = more than half a revi'it (Shulchan Arukh OC 612, via the Denver Kollel / dafyomi sources), person-dependent. The kotevet and the kortov are NOT included: no sourced value yet. The time of a peras (4 to 9 minutes by various opinions) is not drawn. buys: The minimum cup of wine for kiddush: a revi'it, of which one must drink a cheekful, most of a revi'it (Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 271:13).
The same revi'it is the minimum amount of drinking for havdalah, for mitzvot and for transgressions (see Drinking measures).
The oil that the metzora brings on the eighth day: one log (Leviticus 14:10). The priest sprinkles from it seven times and puts it on the metzora (Negaim 14:10).
The minimum dough that must have challah separated: five-fourths of a kav of flour (Challah 2:6).
Ten kav of wisdom descended to the world: Eretz Yisrael took nine and the rest of the world one. So too beauty, wealth, poverty and arrogance (Kiddushin 49b).
A person prefers a kav of his own produce to nine kav of another's (Rav Kahana, Bava Metzia 38a).
One who had a seminal emission is purified by nine kav of water poured over him (Berakhot 22a).
The minimum for a mikveh: forty se'ah of water, about 311 liters or 82 US gallons, the contents of a bit more than one and a half bathtubs (Mikvaot 1:7).
The poor person's sin offering: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour (Leviticus 5:11).
The flour for a meal offering is counted in tenths of an ephah: a tenth with a lamb, two tenths with a ram, three tenths with a bull (Numbers 15:4-9; Menachot 9:1).

A bailee who returns different produce deducts the standard decrease per kor: for wheat and rice nine half-kav, for barley and millet nine kav, for spelt and flaxseed three se'ah (Bava Metzia 3:7; Bava Metzia 40a).
The sum that counts for betrothal according to Beit Hillel; it is one eighth of an Italian issar (Kiddushin 1:1).
The price of the loaf that must be given to a poor person who is passing through, when four se'ah of wheat cost a sela (Peah 8:7).
A husband who feeds his wife through an agent must also give her a silver ma'ah for her other needs (Ketubot 5:9).
The price of a se'ah of wheat in a cheap year: four se'ah cost a sela, which is four dinar (Peah 8:7).
The sum for betrothal according to Beit Shammai (Kiddushin 1:1).
A wife's clothing for a year: fifty dinars (Ketubot 5:8).
A virgin's ketubah: two hundred dinars (Ketubot 1:2).
Half a sela, which is two dinar.
Four se'ah of wheat in a cheap year (Peah 8:7).
A widow's ketubah: one hundred dinars, a maneh (Ketubot 1:2).
Worth twenty-five silver dinar (Bartenura on Bava Metzia 5:1; Rashi on Ketubot 93a).
Drawn about twice the size of a silver dinar and half the size of a sela, since gold was worth roughly twelve times as much as silver by weight.
The depth at which a pit can kill: ten tefachim (BK 5:5).
A fence four cubits high: a fire that crosses it is not the owner's liability (BK 6:4).
How far a fire is held to travel: sixteen cubits according to Rabbi Eliezer, fifty according to Rabbi Akiva (BK 6:4).
The space of ground in which one sows a se'ah of seed: 2,500 square cubits, fifty by fifty (Kehati on BK 6:2).
What is appraised when an animal damages a field: a beit se'ah of it, before and after (BK 6:2).
Rabbi Elazar ben Azaria: judge how far the fire reaches as if the owner stood in the middle of a beit kor (BK 6:4).
Half a sela, which is two dinar.
Five sela of thread is the weight of warp a wife must spin in Judea (Ketubot 5:9).
A maneh of fig cakes is part of a wife's weekly food (Ketubot 5:8).
Equal to 133 and a third amot, a fifteenth of a mil (Shita Mekubetzet on Bava Metzia 32b; other readings exist).
2,000 amot (Halachipedia, Distance of Mil). The distance a person may walk from town on Shabbat, the techum Shabbat.
About eighteen minutes' walk (Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 459:2); some say 22.5 or 24 minutes (Biur Halakha).
Four mil. An average person walks ten parsot, forty mil, in a day (the Gemara, as quoted in the Arukh HaShulchan, Orach Chayim 459:5).
The oil mixed into a meal offering: a quarter of a hin with a lamb, a third with a ram, a half with a bull (Numbers 15:4-9).
Bigger than an olive and smaller than an egg (Tosafot, Eruvin 80b). According to the Rambam it is a third of an egg (Kessef Mishneh on Rambam, Shabbat 8:4). The opinions differ, so no ratio is shown.
R. Chaim Naeh: 19.2 cc.
The minimum for carrying out food on Shabbat is a dried fig (Mishnah Shabbat 7:4).
The minimum amount of eating for mitzvot and for transgressions.
Half a beitzah according to Rashi and Tosafot; a third of a beitzah according to the Rambam.
The measure of food that can transmit tumah (ritual impurity).
R. Chaim Naeh: 54 cc (Shiurei Tzion); his earlier figure was 57.6 cc, with the shell (Shiurei Torah).
The amount of drink that makes one liable for drinking on Yom Kippur (Yoma 80a). It depends on the person, so this figure is only a guide.
For an average person, a little more than half a revi'it (Tosafot, Pesachim 107a; Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 612). The chart shows 1.5 fl oz, about .52 of a revi'it.
According to the Mishnah Berurah (Beur Halakha, Orach Chayim 271) it is about 1.7 to 1.8 fl oz, about .6 of a revi'it.
The minimum amount of drinking for kiddush, for mitzvot and for transgressions.
A beitzah and a half (Halachipedia); a quarter of a log (Rif on Pesachim 23b).
R. Chaim Naeh: 86.4 cc, about 2.9 fl oz (the figure generally accepted); his Shiurei Tzion figure is 81 cc.
The time it takes to eat this amount (“kedei achilat peras”) measures how long a person may stay in a house with tzara’at before becoming impure.
It is also the time in which one must eat for smaller portions, each less than a zayit, to combine into a full zayit.
The shiur is the time, not the volume: this picture shows the amount of bread, not the time (about four to nine minutes).

A plump date (kotevet haGasa, כותבת הגסה): smaller than an egg and larger than two olives (Keritot 14a; Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 612:1). This does not fit Rashi, for whom two olives are the size of an egg. In practice it is close to an egg. The opinions differ, so no ratio is shown.
The minimum amount of food for which one is liable for eating on Yom Kippur (Mishnah Yoma 8:2).
